reason: _produce_provider_turn's cleanup decided it still owned a failed turn when the turn's execution claim equalled the run's; after _stream_tool_turn had recorded FAILED and released the claim, both were None, so the cleanup rewrote FAILED and, if a 'Finish the answer' retry had already moved the turn to FINALIZING, failed the retry. PreparedChat now records a released claim and the cleanup skips a turn its run gave back. This also removes the flake in test_final_answer_retry_resumes_synthesis_through_admission (revision conflict 11/12). Selected: the throughput suite with the new deterministic regression test and the formerly flaky test, plus stream follow, admission cleanup and reconnection suites that cover the producer's terminal path.
exclusions: test_native_hook_turn_ends.py, test_turn_outcome_history.py, test_chat_subagents.py and test_chat_tool_loop.py also exercise this path, but 34 of their cases fail identically on pristine origin/main and with this patch (same failure set; test_chat_tool_loop.py::test_batched_safe_reads_overlap_and_commit_in_provider_order is timing-flaky on both, 2 of 6 runs), so they are not selected. No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed. Real-Core evidence (scratch Postgres Core on this branch: a final-answer failure retried at once through POST /chat/turns/{id}/resume completes; Stop and normal turns unchanged) is recorded in the PR, not executed by CI.
